thread:
anya: heads-up — onboarding README curl snippet uses REDWOOD_API_KEY but the node sample uses REDWOOD_KEY. copy/paste confusion for new users :eyes:

mike: repro'd this. used the curl example, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, then ran the sample app which reads REDWOOD_KEY -> app sends empty header and gets 401s. then client enters retry loop and hits rate limits. log: `401 Unauthorized -> retrying (1/5)` repeatedly.

rachel: ouch. i think this came from two different PRs landing with different env names. i'll own the README update. plan: pick REDWOOD_API_KEY universal, update node/python samples, add a short "setting env vars" note for windows powershell.

kai: can we also add a one-liner for Windows PowerShell since folks keep getting the quotes wrong? e.g.:

```
# powershell
setx REDWOOD_API_KEY "sk-live-..."
# or for current session
$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = 'sk-live-...'
```

anya: yes please. also add a snippet for reading from process.env in the node sample instead of the hardcoded placeholder. tiny patch to avoid accidental commit of example keys.

mike: small gotcha: our curl example currently escapes quotes like `\"` (bash style) which breaks in powershell. we should provide both variants or clearly label which shell the snippet is for.

rachel: i'll change the curl snippet to show both bash and powershell blocks and switch all samples to `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. will push a draft PR in ~30m.

devex-bot: created issue #4567: "README env var parity + powershell escaping" and linked to docs backlog.

kai: tiny suggestion for retries: add a note in the quickstart about exponential backoff behavior so users understand why a flurry of 401s can look like a hang. maybe link to the SDK retry docs.

anya: agreed. add a one-liner: "If you see repeated 401s after onboarding, check your API key env var name and verify no invisible characters from copy/paste."

mike: QA checklist for PR: 1) unify env var name 2) add powershell snippet 3) mark shells clearly 4) run quickstart locally 5) confirm no test secrets left.

rachel: on it. will @-mention ops for a quick review once the PR is up. :+1:

anya: thanks y'all — this should cut a lot of oncall noise for new signups.
